as_told.title: Younger Dryas comet airburst wiped out a proto-civilization

plain: The idea is that about 12,800 years ago, near the end of the last ice age, Earth passed through the trail of debris from a comet that was breaking apart, and the impacts changed the world. This is known as the Younger Dryas impact hypothesis, named after a sudden cold period of that time. The writer and researcher Graham Hancock lays it out, crediting the Comet Research Group, a team of scientists who study the idea. Michels tells it a little differently: he says it may have been a comet blowing up in the air, coming from the Taurid meteor stream (a stream of space debris Earth crosses each year), and that it may have wiped out an early civilization, crediting Hancock, the researcher Randall Carlson and the ancient Greek philosopher Plato.
